newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-DANCE OF COACHES STARTS EARLY IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DANCE OF COACHES STARTS EARLY IN BRAZIL.

text.p: Brazil's so-called "dance of the coaches" has got off to an exceptionally quick start with the first victim falling less than one week after the start of the Brazilian championship.
Fluminense's new coach Carbone took charge of his first training session on Friday following the dismissal of his predecessor Hugo de Leon Thursday afternoon.

De Leon was shown the door after his team were beaten 4-1 by Palmeiras in their first game last Saturday and then held 1-1 on Wednesday by a Cruzeiro team which played the last half hour with nine men after having two sent off.
De Leon was dismissed before Vasco da Gama and Botafogo had even played a game in the tournament.

The cash-strapped Rio de Janeiro club were relegated from the Brazilian championship last year but saved last month when the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF), despite widespread criticism, decided to reinstate them.

"You can't imagine a Brazilian championship without Fluminense but if they are relegated again this year then they really will have to go to the second division," said Carbone, who became the club's fourth coach this year.
The "dance of the coaches" is the popular term giving to the constant chopping and changing of coaches by Brazilian clubs.
Fluminense still have a long way to go to match Guarani, who employed 10 different coaches last year. This led to president Beto Zini earning the nickname "The Exterminator of the Present."
